mainTopic: How a וסת is set and kept: body signs, days and hours, and how long to separate around an expected period
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the body signs in the משנה that warn a woman her period is coming. It also learns from 'וכן כיוצא בהן' that heaviness, trembling and belching are included. שמואל rules that a day-based וסת is set after two times, a listed body sign after one time, and an unlisted sign after three times. אביי explains that the unlisted signs are food triggers like garlic, onions and pepper. When רב יוסף says he never heard שמואל's rule, אביי reminds him that he taught it himself. He taught it on the words of the חכמים, 'לא לשנות ולא לשלש'. A new משנה then teaches how a habit of bleeding at the start or end of the signs affects טהרות. It also brings the מחלוקת of רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה over how long she must stay apart around a time-based וסת. The גמרא settles conflicting sources about רבי יהודה by splitting between bleeding at the end of the night and at the start of the day. רבא rules like רבי יהודה: she separates for the whole עונה of her וסת, both for טהרות and for her husband. A final משנה teaches that a וסת is set, and removed, only after three times.

steps.title: Explaining 'שופעת': impure blood flowing in the middle of pure blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the משנה's sign 'שופעת'. It means she discharges טמא blood in the middle of a flow of טהור blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a woman who discharges impure blood in the middle of pure blood.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a discussion that started before this section. The גמרא explains what kind of 'flowing' the משנה counts as a sign of a coming period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary bleeding cannot be a 'sign' of bleeding, because it is the bleeding itself. So the גמרא explains the case differently. First she discharges טהור blood (a color that does not make her טמאה), and the טמא blood comes in the middle of it. The earlier flow acts as the warning sign.

keyTerms.meaning: She discharges a flow
Blood of a color that makes a woman טמאה
Blood of a color that does not make her טמאה

phrases.english: Where she discharges impure blood
in the midst of pure blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשׁוֹפַעַת דָּם טָמֵא מִתּוֹךְ דָּם טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation of 'שופעת' that began before this section.
steps.terutzMaskana: שופעת is a sign only when the טמא blood comes in the middle of a טהור flow.

steps.title: What does 'and likewise anything similar' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next sign, the shivers. It then asks what the extra phrase 'וכן כיוצא בהן' comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'or a kind of shuddering, etc.' It also says 'and likewise anything similar to them.' What does that come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next words of the משנה. It asks what extra cases the general phrase at the end of the list is meant to cover. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists specific signs and then adds a general phrase. A general phrase like this must be teaching something. So the גמרא wants to know which extra signs it includes.

keyTerms.meaning: Shivers or feverish shuddering
'And likewise anything similar to them' (a general phrase in the משנה)
'To include what?' The question asked when a phrase seems to add extra cases

phrases.english: Or a type of shuddering, etc.
'And likewise anything like them' —
what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra signs the phrase 'וכן כיוצא בהן' includes.

steps.title: It includes heaviness, trembling, and belching
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא says the phrase includes these signs: a heavy head, heavy limbs, trembling, and belching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: It comes to include a woman whose head feels heavy on her, or whose limbs feel heavy on her, or who trembles, or who belches.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא answers the question. He lists four more physical signs that count like the ones the משנה spelled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These signs are similar to the shivers in the משנה, so they are covered by 'anything like them'. This means they are counted as signs the משנה itself includes. Keep this in mind, because it becomes the basis for אביי's challenge in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Her head feels heavy on her
She trembles
She belches

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה בר עולא, heaviness, trembling, and belching are already included in the משנה through 'וכן כיוצא בהן'.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
To include a woman whose head is heavy upon her,
or her limbs are heavy upon her,
or she trembles, or belches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא לְאֵתוֹיֵי אִשָּׁה שֶׁרֹאשָׁהּ כָּבֵד עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase includes a heavy head, heavy limbs, trembling, and belching.

steps.title: How many times sets a cycle: two, one, or three
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a rule. A day-based cycle needs two times. A body-sign cycle listed by the חכמים needs one time. Signs the חכמים did not list need three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said in the name of שמואל: They said that for days, two times are needed. For body-sign cycles, once is enough. For signs the חכמים did not list, three times are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל teaches how many times something must happen before a woman has a fixed cycle (וסת קבוע). The number depends on the type of cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cycle based on dates or intervals needs two times. A cycle based on a sign listed by the חכמים is set after one time. Signs the חכמים did not list are weaker signs, so they need three times. The phrase 'what the חכמים did not list' leads straight into the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: An expected time or sign of a woman's period
For cycles based on days, meaning dates or intervals
Signs the חכמים did not list

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for how a woman's fixed cycle is set in each type of case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya said that Shmuel said:
They said: for days — two,
phrases.notes: Bleeding twice on the same date, or after the same gap of days, sets a cycle.

phrases.english: for body-sign cycles — one,
for what the Sages did not list — three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ לְיָמִים שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about how many times it takes to set each kind of cycle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A day-based cycle needs two times, a listed body sign needs one time, and an unlisted sign needs three times.

steps.title: Which signs are 'not listed by the חכמים'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which signs שמואל means by 'what the חכמים did not list'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For what the Sages did not list': what does that come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which signs fall into שמואל's three-time group. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave the three-time group a name but did not give examples. The גמרא needs to know which real signs belong in it.

phrases.english: 'For what the Sages did not list.'
What does it come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַה שֶּׁלֹּא מָנוּ חֲכָמִים לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase in שמואל's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which signs make up the unlisted, three-time group.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the heaviness and trembling signs
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the unlisted signs are a heavy head, heavy limbs, trembling, and belching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It comes to include a woman whose head feels heavy on her, or whose limbs feel heavy on her, or who trembles, or who belches.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that the three-time group is the same set of signs רבה בר עולא named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף reasons that the משנה does not spell these signs out by name. So he counts them as 'not listed', and by his view they would need three times to set a cycle.

keyTerms.meaning: Her limbs feel heavy

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
To include where her head is heavy upon her,
or her limbs are heavy upon her,
or she trembles, or belches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף לְאֵתוֹיֵי רֹאשָׁהּ כָּבֵד עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The unlisted signs are heaviness, trembling, and belching.

steps.title: אביי: those signs are already in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. רבה בר עולא already showed that the משנה includes those signs, so they cannot be 'unlisted'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is this teaching us? It is already in the משנה! רבה בר עולא explained that the משנה includes these signs.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer. The signs רב יוסף named are already part of the משנה through 'וכן כיוצא בהן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since step 3 showed that the משנה includes these signs, they are 'listed' signs, and one time should be enough for them. Counting them as the unlisted group adds nothing new and contradicts the משנה. So שמואל must mean other signs.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is this teaching us?' It challenges a statement as adding nothing new
'It is already in the משנה!'
He explained it

steps.confusionAlert: Signs that the משנה covers only through 'anything like them' still count as listed by the חכמים. 'Listed' does not only mean named word for word.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
What is this teaching us?
It is the mishna!
For Rabba bar Ulla explained it.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 3, where רבה בר עולא explained the phrase 'וכן כיוצא בהן'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן מַתְנִיתִין הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that heaviness and trembling are the unlisted signs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already includes these signs through 'וכן כיוצא בהן', so they are listed signs, and naming them adds nothing.

steps.title: אביי: garlic, onions, or pepper before bleeding
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives his own answer. The unlisted signs are seeing blood after eating garlic, eating onions, or chewing pepper.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It comes to include a woman who ate garlic and saw blood, ate onions and saw blood, or chewed pepper and saw blood.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב יוסף's answer was rejected, אביי offers a new answer. The unlisted group is about foods that bring on bleeding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are outside triggers, not body feelings like the signs in the משנה, so the משנה does not include them at all. That is why they need three times before they set a cycle. This gives שמואל's rule real new content.

keyTerms.meaning: Garlic
Onions
She chewed pepper
She saw blood

steps.whatToRemember: A sign listed in the משנה, including through 'anything like them', sets a cycle after one time. A food trigger like garlic, onions, or pepper sets a cycle only after three times (אביי).

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
To include where she ate garlic and saw blood,
or ate onions and saw blood,
or chewed pepper and saw blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי לְאֵתוֹיֵי אָכְלָה שׁוּם וְרָאֲתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected answer with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new definition after the old one was rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The unlisted signs are heaviness and trembling (רב יוסף).
steps.terutzMaskana: The unlisted signs are food triggers: garlic, onions, and pepper, which need three times.

steps.title: רב יוסף says he never heard this teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he does not know the rule of שמואל that the discussion has been built on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I never heard this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף announces that he does not recognize שמואל's rule from Step 4. This sets up the next move, where אביי will remind him that he taught it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now everyone assumed שמואל's rule was known: days need two times, listed body signs need one, unlisted signs need three. Now רב יוסף, who was just answering questions about it, says the rule itself is new to him. This opens a short side story about where the rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or tradition that was heard and passed on
I did not hear it; I do not know this tradition

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I did not hear this teaching.
phrases.notes: He means שמואל's rule from earlier: two times for days, one time for listed body signs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the unlisted signs back to the question of whether שמואל's rule is known at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף does not recognize שמואל's rule about how many times are needed to set a וסת.

steps.title: אביי reminds רב יוסף of the משנה where he taught it
steps.stepSummary: אביי says: you told us this yourself, on the משנה about a woman whose usual day moved from the 15th to the 20th.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You told it to us, and you told it to us on this משנה. If a woman usually saw blood on day 15 and changed to day 20, both days are forbidden. If she saw on day 20 three times, day 15 becomes permitted and day 20 is now her set day, because a woman does not set a וסת until she sets it three times.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins proving that רב יוסף himself taught this rule. First he names the משנה it was taught on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a new day becomes a set וסת only after three times. That seems to clash with שמואל's rule that days need only two times. This clash is the background for what רב יוסף taught on this משנה, which אביי quotes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's set, expected time for her period
Sets or fixes (a וסת)
She changed (her usual pattern)
Both this day and that day are forbidden
Became permitted

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
You yourself told it to us,
and it was on this that you told it to us:

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: If she was used to seeing blood on the fifteenth day,
and she changed to the twentieth day,
both this day and that day are forbidden.
If she changed to the twentieth day three times,
the fifteenth day becomes permitted,
and she has set the twentieth day for herself,
because a woman does not set a וסת for herself
until she sets it three times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב יוסף's claim by pointing to the משנה where he taught the rule.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יוסף did hear and teach שמואל's rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a woman whose day moved from the 15th to the 20th, where רב יוסף taught it.

steps.title: שמואל says the משנה follows one view and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רב יוסף quoting שמואל: the משנה follows רבן גמליאל בר רבי, but the חכמים say she needs neither 'לשנות' nor 'לשלש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you told us about it: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This is the view of רבן גמליאל בר רבי, who said it in the name of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. But the חכמים say: once she saw, she does not need to repeat a second time or a third time.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues quoting what רב יוסף taught on this משנה. According to שמואל, the 'three times' rule is only one opinion, and the חכמים require fewer times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the clash with שמואל's rule: the משנה's 'three times' is not the final view. The חכמים say she does not need 'לשנות' or 'לשלש'. Why both words are needed is what the students ask next.

keyTerms.meaning: To do it a second time (to repeat once)
To do it a third time
The Sages, the majority view that disagrees here

phrases.english: And you told us about it,
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי,
phrases.english: This is the view of Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
but the Sages say:
Once she saw, she does not need
to repeat a second time, nor to repeat a third time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the teaching רב יוסף said on the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's 'three times' follows רבן גמליאל בר רבי; the חכמים say she needs neither 'לשנות' nor 'לשלש'.

steps.title: The students ask why 'third time' needs saying
steps.stepSummary: The students challenged רב יוסף: if a second time is not needed, obviously a third is not needed either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said to you: You told us she need not repeat a second time; is it necessary to say she need not repeat a third time?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי recalls the question the students asked רב יוסף back then. They asked why the חכמים mention the third time at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she does not even need a second time, then a third time is already ruled out. So the word 'לשלש' seems extra. This forces an explanation of what each word refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it needed? (meaning: this is obvious, why say it?)

phrases.english: And we said to you:
You told us she need not repeat a second time; is a third time even worth saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the חכמים's statement just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'לא לשנות ולא לשלש' in the חכמים's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even a second time is unnecessary, a third time is unnecessary too, so 'לשלש' seems extra.

steps.title: רב יוסף had explained: one word for body signs, one for days
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף had answered that 'לשנות' refers to body-sign cycles and 'לשלש' refers to day cycles. This is exactly שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you told us: 'Not a second time' is about body-sign cycles; 'not a third time' is about day cycles.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his reminder with רב יוסף's own answer. This answer is the very rule רב יוסף said he never heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word covers a different kind of cycle. For a body-sign cycle, she does not need a second time, so one time sets it. For a day cycle, she does not need a third time, so two times set it. That matches שמואל's rule from Step 4, so אביי has proven that רב יוסף taught it.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: cycles set by a body sign (like yawning or sneezing)
Here: cycles set by a day count

steps.whatToRemember: The source of שמואל's rule is the חכמים's words 'לא לשנות ולא לשלש': body signs need one time, days need two.
steps.confusionAlert: 'לא לשנות' does not mean 'she must not repeat'. It means she does not need a second time, so one time is enough. 'לא לשלש' means she does not need a third time, so two times are enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows where שמואל's rule comes from and closes the side story: רב יוסף had taught the rule himself and forgot it.

phrases.english: And you told us:
'A second time' is about body-sign cycles; 'a third time' is about day cycles.
phrases.notes: So a body-sign cycle is set after one time, and a day cycle after two times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question and, in doing so, proves that רב יוסף taught שמואל's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two words between two kinds of cycles
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לשנות' and 'לשלש' both refer to the same kind of cycle, so 'לשלש' is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לשנות' refers to body-sign cycles (one time is enough), and 'לשלש' refers to day cycles (two times are enough).

steps.title: Why not credit the משנה to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל tied the משנה to רבן גמליאל בר רבי. He could have simply said it follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let שמואל say: this משנה is the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how שמואל phrased his statement. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is already known to require three times to set a pattern, so why bring in a different name?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, שמואל said the משנה follows רבן גמליאל בר רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the well-known source for needing a pattern three times. So the גמרא asks why שמואל used a less obvious name when a familiar one was available.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him say (why not just say...)

phrases.english: But let him say: this is the statement of
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel!
phrases.notes: He is the one known for saying a pattern needs three times to be set.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵימָא: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of שמואל's statement that was just confirmed as his rule
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's choice to credit the משנה to רבן גמליאל בר רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler and better-known source, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, already holds that three times are needed. So naming רבן גמליאל בר רבי seems unnecessary.

steps.title: שמואל teaches that רבן גמליאל בר רבי agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: שמואל chose that name on purpose. He wanted to teach that רבן גמליאל בר רבי holds the same view as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what שמואל is teaching us: that רבן גמליאל, son of רבי, holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. שמואל's wording adds new information: another תנא shares this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming רבן גמליאל בר רבי is not extra. It tells us that this later תנא also agrees with requiring three times. Without שמואל's statement, we would not have known that.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is teaching us
He holds (this opinion)
Son of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's wording teaches that רבן גמליאל בר רבי agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that a pattern needs three times.

phrases.english: This is what Shmuel teaches us:
that Rabban Gamliel, son of Rabbi,

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: holds like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about שמואל's wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: New information: the wording teaches that another תנא agrees
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming רבן גמליאל בר רבי seemed pointless, since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was the obvious source
steps.terutzMaskana: The name was chosen to teach that רבן גמליאל בר רבי holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

steps.title: משנה: bleeding at the start or the end of the body-sign וסת
steps.stepSummary: Suppose a woman usually bleeds at the start of her body-sign וסת. Then טהרות she handled during that time are impure. If she usually bleeds at the end, they stay pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman usually sees blood at the beginning of her body signs, all the pure items she handled during the signs are impure. If she usually sees blood at the end of the signs, all the pure items she handled during the signs are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is about a woman whose וסת comes with physical signs, and what happens to pure items she touched while those signs were going on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she usually bleeds right when the signs begin, we assume the bleeding started from the beginning. So whatever she handled during the signs becomes impure. If she usually bleeds only when the signs end, then whatever she handled earlier, during the signs, stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, the משנה
Used to (an established habit)
Cycles; here, the physical signs that come with her period
Items that must be kept ritually pure

phrases.english: MISHNA: If she was accustomed
to see blood at the beginning of the cycle signs —
all the pure items that she handled
during the cycle signs are impure.
If she usually saw at the end of the cycle signs —
all the pure items that she handled
during the cycle signs are pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה בִּתְחִלַּת הַוְּסָתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה opens a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her usual habit decides the status of טהרות handled during the body signs: impure if she usually bleeds at the start, pure if she usually bleeds at the end.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: days and hours also set a וסת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says a וסת can also be set by a particular day and hour. If she usually bleeds at sunrise, she is forbidden only at sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: days and hours also set a וסת. If she usually sees blood at sunrise, she is forbidden only at sunrise.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יוסי. He adds that time, meaning a certain day and hour, can also set a וסת, and he gives an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says the time of day counts as part of the וסת. So the time she must stay apart from her husband is narrow: only the hour she expects to bleed. In this case that is sunrise.

keyTerms.meaning: Days and hours
Sunrise
Forbidden (to be intimate with her husband)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף יָמִים וְשָׁעוֹת וְסָתוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: days and hours are also cycles.
If she was accustomed to see blood
at sunrise —
she is forbidden only
phrases.notes: Forbidden here means being intimate with her husband.

phrases.english: at sunrise.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף יָמִים וְשָׁעוֹת וְסָתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds time-based וסתות to the body-sign וסתות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A set hour counts as a וסת, and she is forbidden only during that hour.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the whole day is hers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי יוסי about how far the restriction reaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the whole day is hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יהודה's view about the woman who usually bleeds at sunrise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the explanation of this משנה, once sunrise passes and she has not bled, she is permitted for the rest of that day. רבי יהודה still forbids the night before, which רבי יוסי permits. The ברייתא in the coming steps makes their מחלוקת clearer.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole day
Is hers (belongs to her as a time of permission)
A dispute between sages

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַיּוֹם שֶׁלָּהּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the whole day is hers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַיּוֹם שֶׁלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion on the time-based וסת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once sunrise passes without bleeding, the rest of the day is permitted.

steps.title: ברייתא asks: how does רבי יוסי's time-based וסת work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It opens by asking for the case that רבי יוסי meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: how did רבי יוסי say that days and hours set a וסת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It brings a ברייתא that asks for a concrete case, which sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said only 'days and hours are also וסתות.' The ברייתא wants a real example so we can see exactly what רבי יוסי means.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא
How? In what case?
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
How did Rabbi Yosei say
that days and hours are cycles?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי יָמִים וְשָׁעוֹת וְסָתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a clear case behind רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of a וסת set by a day and an hour

steps.title: The case: day 20 at the sixth hour, and רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: She bled twice on day 20 at the sixth hour. Day 20 comes again and she has not bled. רבי יהודה forbids her for all of the first six hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: She usually saw blood on day 20 and again on day 20, at the sixth hour and again at the sixth hour. Day 20 came and she did not see blood. רבי יהודה says she is forbidden to be with her husband for all of the first six hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the case. It then states רבי יהודה's opinion about how long she must stay apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the וסת is set by both a day (the 20th) and an hour (the sixth). רבי יהודה is stricter: he forbids the whole stretch of time from the start of the day up to and including the sixth hour.

keyTerms.meaning: To be intimate with her husband
Six hours; here, the sixth hour of the day
The first ones

phrases.english: If she was accustomed to see blood
on the twentieth day and again on the twentieth day,
and at the sixth hour and again at the sixth hour.
The twentieth day arrived and she did not see —
she is forbidden to be with her husband
for all of the first six hours,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה מִיּוֹם עֶשְׂרִים לְיוֹם עֶשְׂרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question with a concrete case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A וסת set on day 20 at the sixth hour. רבי יהודה forbids all of the first six hours of that day.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: permitted until the sixth hour
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי permits her until the sixth hour. She needs to be concerned only during the sixth hour itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי permits until the sixth hour, and she must be concerned at the sixth hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with רבי יוסי's more lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי treats the hour as the real וסת. So only the expected hour is forbidden, not the hours before it. This fits his words in the משנה: 'she is forbidden only at sunrise.'

keyTerms.meaning: Permits
She must be concerned (and stay apart)
Until

steps.whatToRemember: For a time-based וסת, רבי יהודה forbids from the start of the day until the expected hour. רבי יוסי forbids only the expected hour itself.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר עַד שֵׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei permits until the sixth hour,
and she is concerned at the sixth hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר עַד שֵׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי's side of the מחלוקת in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the expected hour itself is forbidden; the hours before it are permitted.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: after six hours with no bleeding, she is still forbidden all day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If the six hours pass and she has not bled, רבי יהודה still forbids relations for the entire day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If six hours passed and she did not see blood, she is forbidden to have relations the whole day. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא carries on with the same case: her וסת is the sixth hour of day 20. Now the sixth hour has passed with no bleeding, and רבי יהודה says she stays forbidden for the rest of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20, רבי יהודה stretched the restriction backward to cover the six hours before the וסת. Here he stretches it forward too. Even after the expected time passes with no blood, the whole day stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: To have marital relations
Six hours, meaning the first half of the day up to the time of her וסת
The entire day

phrases.english: If six hours passed and she did not see blood,
phrases.notes: This is the same woman from Step 20, whose וסת is the sixth hour of day 20.

phrases.english: she is forbidden to have relations the entire day,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and moves the case to after the time of the וסת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, even after the וסת time passes with no bleeding, relations are forbidden for the whole day.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: permitted from the afternoon onward
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי permits relations once the sixth hour is over, from מנחה time and onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי permits her from מנחה time onward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers רבי יהודה for the time after the וסת. Once the sixth hour is over, she is allowed again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches what רבי יוסי said in Step 21. The concern sits only on the exact hour of the וסת, both before it and after it. So the restriction ends as soon as that hour ends.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits
Afternoon time, here meaning the start of the seventh hour
And onward (literally, 'and upward')

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה stretches the restriction to the whole day: the six hours before the וסת and the rest of the day after it. רבי יוסי limits it to the exact hour of the וסת.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei permits
from מנחה time onward.
phrases.notes: Since her וסת was the sixth hour, מנחה time here means right when the seventh hour begins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי's opposing view to רבי יהודה's ruling in Step 22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, once the hour of the וסת passes, relations are permitted from מנחה time onward.

steps.title: A clash: is the night before a sunrise period forbidden or allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a woman used to bleeding at sunrise, where רבי יהודה forbids the night before. It then challenges this with a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says 'the whole night is hers.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה speaks of a woman who 'was accustomed' to see blood at sunrise. But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, the whole night is hers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of a woman whose וסת is at sunrise. There, רבי יהודה forbids the night before. Then it raises a ברייתא that has רבי יהודה permitting that whole night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources quote the same תנא, רבי יהודה, about the same kind of woman. Yet one forbids the night before sunrise and the other permits it. The גמרא needs a way to fit the two together.

keyTerms.meaning: Accustomed, used to (here, used to bleeding at a set time)
The whole night is hers, meaning she is permitted all night

phrases.english: She was accustomed.
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the משנה's case of a woman used to bleeding at sunrise. There, רבי יהודה forbids the night before.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The whole night is hers!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא back to the משנה and raises a contradiction about רבי יהודה's view
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's report that רבי יהודה forbids the night before a sunrise וסת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה as permitting the whole night, which goes straight against the משנה.

steps.title: Two different timings: right after sunrise versus right before it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא speaks of a woman who bleeds at the start of the day. The משנה speaks of a woman who bleeds at the very end of the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This source is where she usually sees at the beginning of the day, and that source is where she usually sees at the end of the night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clears up the clash by showing that the two sources describe two different women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her וסת is just after sunrise, it falls in the daytime, so the night before is free. If her וסת is just before sunrise, it falls at the end of the night, so the night is forbidden. Both sources follow the same רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, meaning both sources can be true
Used to, accustomed
Day (Aramaic)
Night (Aramaic)

steps.confusionAlert: The two הָא's are easy to mix up. The first הָא, which says the night is allowed, is the ברייתא, about a woman who bleeds at the start of the day. The second הָא, which says the night is forbidden, is the משנה, about a woman who bleeds at the end of the night.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where she usually sees at the beginning of the day,
phrases.notes: This first one is the ברייתא that permits the night.

phrases.english: and that is where she usually sees at the end of the night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two sources deal with different timings of the וסת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the two sources quote רבי יהודה ruling in opposite ways on the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: A וסת right after sunrise leaves the night permitted. A וסת right before sunrise makes the night forbidden.

steps.title: One ברייתא: רבי יהודה forbids before the period and permits after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה forbids relations before the time of her וסת and permits them after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה forbids her before her וסת and permits her after her וסת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins presenting two ברייתות about רבי יהודה's view. This first one is setting up a contradiction that will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יהודה stretches the restriction only backward, to the time before the וסת. Once the time passes with no bleeding, she is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's fixed time for bleeding
Forbids her
Before the time of her וסת

phrases.english: One ברייתא teaches:
Rabbi Yehuda forbids her before her וסת,
and permits her after her וסת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of sources about רבי יהודה's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this ברייתא, רבי יהודה forbids relations before the וסת and permits them after it.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the opposite: forbidden after, permitted before
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא reports רבי יהודה's view the opposite way. He forbids after the וסת and permits before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another ברייתא teaches: he forbids her after her וסת and permits her before her וסת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the second ברייתא right next to the first. The two plainly contradict each other, and this sets up a resolution that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות speak in the name of רבי יהודה, yet they flip which side of the וסת is forbidden. This sharpens the question of what רבי יהודה really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one (another ברייתא)
After the time of her וסת
Permits her

phrases.english: And another ברייתא teaches:
he forbids her after her וסת,
and permits her before her וסת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places an opposite report against the ברייתא in Step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in Step 26 that has רבי יהודה forbidding before the וסת and permitting after
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא reports רבי יהודה's view exactly reversed, so the two cannot both be true as they stand.

steps.title: Two ברייתות, two different times of seeing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the clash between the two ברייתות about רבי יהודה. One speaks of a woman who sees at the end of the night, the other of a woman who sees at the start of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. One ברייתא speaks of a woman who usually sees blood at the end of the night. The other speaks of a woman who usually sees blood at the start of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 27. It shows that the two ברייתות are not arguing about רבי יהודה's view. They are simply talking about two different women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she sees at the end of the night, her וסת falls in the night עונה. So the earlier part of that same night, before her וסת, is forbidden. If she sees at the start of the day, her וסת falls in the day עונה. So the rest of that day, after her וסת, is forbidden, while the night before is a separate עונה and stays permitted. Either way, רבי יהודה forbids the whole עונה in which her וסת falls.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really clash
She is used to seeing blood at a set time
The end of the night
The beginning of the day

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful which ברייתא goes with which case. 'End of the night' explains the ברייתא that forbids BEFORE the וסת. 'Start of the day' explains the ברייתא that forbids AFTER it.

phrases.english: And it is not difficult:
this one is where she is used to seeing at the end of the night,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that forbids before the וסת, because the earlier part of that same night is forbidden.

phrases.english: that one is where she is used to seeing at the start of the day.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that forbids after the וסת, because the rest of that day is still the same עונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא describes a different time of seeing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to report opposite views of רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow one rule: the whole עונה of her וסת is forbidden, whether that part comes before or after the moment she sees.

steps.title: רבא rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a final ruling in the argument: we follow רבי יהודה, who forbids the whole עונה of her וסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is stricter than רבי יוסי's view from Step 23. The next step will check whether this ruling fits another statement of רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion

phrases.english: Rava said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After making רבי יהודה's view consistent, the גמרא brings a ruling that follows it.

steps.title: Did רבא really say that? His 'one עונה' ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from a ברייתא and from his own words that a couple separates for one עונה before the וסת. This seems to mean an extra time-block, which is more than רבי יהודה requires.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say this? But a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity.' From here רבי ירמיה said this is a warning to the Jewish people to separate from their wives close to their וסת. How close? רבא said: one עונה. Doesn't that mean an extra עונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבא could really rule like רבי יהודה. It quotes another statement of his that seems to require more separation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עונה is a twelve-hour block, either the day or the night. If רבא's 'one עונה' means an additional block before the עונה of the וסת, he is stricter than רבי יהודה, who forbids only the עונה of the וסת itself. Then his two statements would contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (opens a challenge)
A warning, a prohibition taken from a פסוק
Close to the time of their expected period
A twelve-hour block: either the day or the night
Doesn't it mean...? (pushes a reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree on the words 'one עונה.' The whole question is whether this means an EXTRA block before her וסת, or the block of the וסת itself.

phrases.english: And did Rava say so?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
"You shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity" —
From here Rabbi Yirmeya said:
a warning to the children of Israel
that they should separate from their wives close to their cycle.
And how much? Rava said: one onah.
phrases.notes: An עונה is a whole day or a whole night.

phrases.english: Is it not referring to another onah?
phrases.notes: He means an extra twelve hours before the עונה of her וסת, which would be stricter than רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in Step 29 using another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's 'one עונה' seems to add an extra block before the וסת, which goes beyond רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: It means the same עונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא's 'one עונה' is the עונה of the וסת itself, not an extra one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means that same עונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading of the question. רבא meant only the עונה in which the וסת falls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, רבא's measure is exactly רבי יהודה's view: the whole day or night of the וסת is forbidden. So his two statements agree.

keyTerms.meaning: That same עונה, the one in which her וסת falls

phrases.english: No, that same onah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'One עונה' meant an extra block before the וסת.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One עונה' is the עונה of the וסת itself, which matches רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why did רבא need to say it twice?
steps.stepSummary: Since both statements now say the same thing, the גמרא asks why רבא needed both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need two statements?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both of רבא's statements mean the same thing, the גמרא asks why he said both. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Follow רבי יהודה' and 'one עונה, the same one' now teach the same rule. The גמרא expects each statement to add something new, so it asks what the extra one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need two statements?

phrases.english: And why do I need two?
phrases.notes: Both of רבא's statements: 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה' and 'one עונה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in Step 31, which made the two statements match.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of רבא's two statements adds.

steps.title: Both are needed: pure items versus her husband
steps.stepSummary: Both statements are needed. From 'follow רבי יהודה' alone, one might have limited it to handling pure items (טהרות). The second statement teaches that it applies to her husband too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If he had taught only this one, I would have said it applies only to pure items (טהרות), but not to her husband. So he teaches us that it applies to her husband too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that each statement has its own job. The 'one עונה' statement shows that the ruling also covers relations with her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Follow רבי יהודה' could have been read as being only about טהרות, while for her husband we would follow רבי יוסי's easier view. The 'separate from their wives' statement makes clear that רבי יהודה's measure applies to marital relations as well.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; each statement teaches something
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
Pure items that must be kept away from טומאה
It teaches us (the point of the extra statement)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: a couple separates for the whole עונה (day or night) in which her וסת falls, and not more. This applies both to טהרות and to her husband.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical rule for how long a couple separates around an expected period.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if he had taught us only this one —
phrases.notes: 'This one' is רבא's ruling in Step 29 that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: I would have said: these words apply to pure items,
but for her husband — no.
So he teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second statement shows that רבי יהודה's measure also covers relations with her husband, not only טהרות.

steps.title: Why the second statement alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If רבא had only said 'separate one עונה before the וסת,' we might think that means an extra time-block. So he also said 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה,' which shows it means only the עונה of the וסת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רבא had taught only that other statement, I would have thought that 'close to her וסת' means an additional time-block. So he teaches us that it means that same time-block.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from the last step by showing the other side: why the statement 'follow רבי יהודה' was also needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 showed why 'one עונה before the וסת' was needed: to include her husband. Now the גמרא shows the reverse. On its own, 'one עונה before' sounds like an extra block of time. Pairing it with 'הלכה כרבי יהודה' shows it means only the עונה of the וסת itself.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
It comes to teach us
Close to (right before) her expected period
Another, extra time-block (a day or a night)

steps.whatToRemember: Each of רבא's two statements fills a gap in the other. 'Follow רבי יהודה' limits the time to just the עונה of the וסת. 'One עונה before' widens who it applies to: her husband, and not only טהרות.

phrases.english: And if [we had only] that one,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is רבא's other statement, 'separate one עונה before her וסת.'

phrases.english: I would have said
that 'close to her וסת' means an additional time-block.
So it teaches us: that same time-block.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the צריכא answer begun in step 33
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The statement 'follow רבי יהודה' is needed so we don't read 'one עונה before' as an extra time-block.

steps.title: A changed day: both the old and new days are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that if a woman used to see blood on day 15 and changed to day 20, both days are forbidden. Even after the change happens twice, both days are still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If she was used to seeing blood on the fifteenth day and changed to seeing it on the twentieth day, both days are forbidden. If she changed to the twentieth day twice, both days are still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a woman whose regular day changes, and rules that one or two changes are not enough to cancel the old day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her old day, 15, is still her fixed וסת, so she must keep it. The new day, 20, has now shown up, so she must watch for it too. After one or two changes, nothing has been settled yet, so both days stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (our משנה)
A woman's regular, expected time for her period
She changed (her pattern shifted)
Both this one and that one are forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Seeing on the new day does not cancel the old day. After one or two changes she must be careful on BOTH days.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: If she was accustomed
to see [blood] on the fifteenth day,
and she changed to seeing it on the twentieth day,
this and that are both forbidden.
If she changed twice to the twentieth day,
this and that are both forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous sugya ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After one or two changes to a new day, both the old fixed day and the new day are forbidden.

steps.title: After three times the new day is fixed and the old day is released
steps.stepSummary: If she changes to day 20 three times, day 15 becomes permitted and day 20 becomes her fixed וסת. The reason is that a וסת is set only by three times, and removed only by three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she changed to the twentieth day three times, the fifteenth becomes permitted and she has fixed the twentieth day for herself. A woman does not set a וסת until she sets it three times, and she is not freed from a וסת until it is uprooted from her three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the case. Three changes are enough to set the new day and to release the old one, and the משנה gives the general rule behind this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number three works in both directions. It takes three times to create a fixed וסת (קביעות), and three misses to remove one (עקירה). After three times on day 20, both things happen at once: day 20 is set and day 15 is uprooted.

keyTerms.meaning: Became permitted
Sets (establishes) a fixed וסת
Three times, the number needed to set or remove a וסת
That it is uprooted (the old וסת stops applying)

steps.whatToRemember: A וסת is set by three times and removed by three times. Until then, the old day still counts and any new day must also be watched.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'three times' rule is the basic principle for setting and removing a וסת in הלכות נדה.

phrases.english: If she changed three times to the twentieth day,
the fifteenth became permitted,
and she has fixed the twentieth day for herself,
because a woman does not set a וסת for herself
until she sets it three times,
and she is not freed from the וסת
until it is uprooted from her three times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with the three-times case and its general rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three times on the new day sets it as her וסת and releases the old day. A וסת is both set and removed only through three times.
